newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen gives up gains.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen gives up gains.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mixed, as the yen relinquished morning gains and slunk back into the minus column.
December yen eroded in the afternoon after failing to clear resistance that one floor technician pegged at the $0.008857 level, or 113.65 spot, during the morning's quick advance.
Floor brokers said the unit sagged under weight of technicals and crosses, especially versus the buoyant mark.
"I think it's mostly cross trading going on -- mark/Swiss, mark/yen, mark/sterling," said one floor broker. "The market's really been whipsawing around."
During the afternoon, when turnover had slowed, December yen futures returned to the $0.008800 level that had formed the contract low set on Monday.
Overnight in electronic trading, it had slumped to another contract low, at $0.008757, before rebounding.
Chartists said yen's weak close boded for more downside.
"The bottom line is that's a real negative close," said one floor broker of the nearby yen, which settled down $0.000007 at $0.008806. "I think we'll see 115.00 soon, if not by the end of the week."
That would equate a drop in nearby yen to $0.008753.
Yen fell overnight after U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin said in a television interview that he did not share concern that the dollar had risen too high.

Marks briefly extended cross-related gains after a news agency report said an EU working group had rejected a proposed transfer of funds from France Telecom to French government finances to help France cut its deficit and meet EMU criteria.
The mark only shaved gains, however, after a French finance ministry official later said no decision had been taken about the transfer.

Marks rose overnight after Germany's six leading economic research institutes said on Tuesday that current German rates were appropriate but that slight tightening was possible if M3 money supply growth stayed above target.
Currencies had muted response to rallies in U.S. debt and stock markets on soft economic data and glossed over comments by Richmond Federal Reserve president Alfred Broaddus.

Dec yen fell $0.00007 to $0.008806, marks rose $0.0043 to $0.6644, Swiss franc up $0.0031 at $0.8004, sterling fell $0.0022 to $1.6092, Can dollar lost $0.0001 to $0.7456, Aussie dollar lost $0.0010 to $0.7896, Mex peso fell $0.001050 to $0.121650. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
